This book is the computational companion to

> Clark, S. J. (2026). *Multi-dimensional Mortality (MDMx)*. arXiv:2603.20518.

It reproduces every figure, table and number in the paper from the Human
Mortality Database, and explains each step of the analysis in more detail
than a journal article can.

## How the book is organised

* **Part I — Data pipeline** (chapters d1–d6, paper §2) takes the HMD
  download to the four-way mortality tensor: verifying the release, reading the files,
  curation, the event dictionary of wars and pandemics, adaptive temporal
  pooling, and assembling the tensor.  Every change made to the published
  data is recorded in `results/ledger/data-changes.csv`.
* **Part II — Analysis** has one chapter per section of the paper's methods and
  results: 04 (the Tucker decomposition, paper §3), 06 (a typology of age patterns, §4),
  07 (reconstruction at arbitrary mortality levels, §5), 08 (exceptional mortality, §6),
  09 (life table fitting, §7), 10 (prediction from summary indicators, §8),
  11 (the two forecasters, §9, and what the flow field says about mortality change,
  §11.4) and 12 (the forecast evaluation, §10).  The chapters' file names keep their
  own numbers (04, 06, …), which do not follow the paper's sections.  Each chapter
  also shows results that the paper leaves out.
* **Appendices** describe the computing environment and show the
  provenance of every result.

## How to read a chapter

Each chapter starts with a box naming the paper sections it reproduces and
the figures and tables it writes.  Code is shown next to the prose that
explains it; the routine machinery lives in the `mdmx` Python package
(`src/mdmx/`), whose functions are documented line by line.

## How results reach the paper

Chapters write figures to `results/figures/`, tables to `results/tables/`
and every number the paper quotes to `results/numbers/` (as LaTeX macros).
The paper reads only those files, so the paper and the book can never
disagree.  `results/manifest.json` records, for every one of these files,
the chapter that produced it and the checksums of its inputs.
